#| include: false

CRAN's build machines have no GPU, so none of the chunks below run when the
package is built; they show the calls to make on your own hardware.

emeans runs the same algorithm on a GPU through the optional
[torch](https://torch.mlverse.org/) package, which needs its LibTorch backend
installed before anything interesting can happen:

```r
install.packages("torch")
torch::install_torch()
```

## What changes on a device

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
inline_svg("devices.svg")
```

* Computation happens in float32 on the device, and on Apple MPS the counts
  and the objective are float32 as well.
* Every random draw still comes from R's generator, so `set.seed()` remains in
  charge of the fit.
* Results will not match the CPU path bit for bit, because float32 rounds
  differently, and on CUDA they may not even match each other between runs,
  since `index_add_` sums with atomics in an order that can vary.
* The result is an ordinary `"emeans"` object holding R matrices and vectors,
  so nothing downstream needs to know a GPU was involved.

## Apple GPUs (MPS)

```{r}
library(emeans)
set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(rnorm(2e6 * 16), ncol = 16)
fit <- emeans(x, 1000, device = "mps")
fit
predict(fit, x[1:10, ])   # assigned on the same device
```

## NVIDIA GPUs (CUDA)

```{r}
fit <- emeans(x, 1000, device = "cuda")       # or "cuda:1"
```

::: {.callout-warning}
The CUDA path is experimental: the torch backend has been tested on Apple
MPS and on torch's CPU device but has yet to meet an NVIDIA card. If you give
it a whirl, please report what you see at
<https://github.com/coatless-rpkg/emeans/issues>.
:::

## Torch on the CPU, and tensors as input

`device = "torch:cpu"` runs the torch backend on the CPU, which is handy for
testing without a GPU. On any torch device `x` may also be a 2-D
`torch_tensor`, which emeans casts to float32 and moves to the device but
does not check for `NA`, `NaN` or infinite values, so make sure it arrives
clean.

```{r}
xt <- torch::torch_tensor(x, device = "mps")
fit <- emeans(xt, 1000, device = "mps")
```
